title: Two async writers of the same store state must guard against each other
rule: When more than one async path writes the same store state (a list refetch for a new sort order, a refresh after an event), each path's 'newest answer wins' guard must also cover the other paths: an answer fetched before another writer's newer write must be dropped or fetched again. One counter per path is not enough — check the other path's counter (or share one) before writing. Add a test that holds the older request with a gate, lets the other writer land, then releases it and asserts the newer state stays.
rationale: E5.4 (#67): after merging main, a sort-order fetch in flight when an activation event landed overwrote refreshActivation's newer families list, because only fetchFamilies bumped listGeneration; the activation dot and row label went back to 'not active'.
